name: Supernotes
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Capture small linked cards, tag them, and review or share focused collections

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Starts with 100 kept cards; +20 cards per successful referral; cards have a 1,200-character soft limit.
tiers.notes: At the card cap, existing kept cards remain viewable and editable, but the user cannot create, like or join new cards.

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.limits: Unlimited cards; full API and integrations; AI features; priority support on yearly billing.
tiers.notes: Source currency is GBP. Monthly is £8, derived exactly from the page's £6 annual equivalent and 25% annual discount; annual is £72/year. Converted at the ECB 2026-08-12 reference cross-rate of about $1.35254/£.

tiers.name: Unlimited 4-Year licence
tiers.limits: Unlimited creation for 4 years; after expiry, existing cards remain readable, editable and shareable, but no new cards can be created.
tiers.notes: Single non-recurring payment with a stated 50% discount; the live public page did not expose the current one-time amount.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 100 kept cards initially; achievements and referrals can raise the cap, with +20 cards per successful referral
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual + one-time 4-year licence; £72 billed annually; 14-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: App Store/Play Store prices and taxes can differ by region; student pricing is 50% off yearly or 63% off the 4-year licence; new-card creation stops when a 4-year licence expires unless renewed

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Supernotes, capture small linked cards, tag them, and review or share focused collections. The hard boundary is real-time collaboration, mobile polish, sync, and card-based workflow refinement, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Capture small linked note cards, tag them into focused collections, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: real-time collaboration, mobile polish, sync, and card-based workflow refinement
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Supernotes because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: Memos
alternatives.desc: Small Markdown cards, tags and public or private sharing, served from one Docker container.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Unlimited plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Supernotes in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture small linked note cards, tag them into focused collections, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
